name: Omeprazole
executiveSummary: Proton pump inhibitor. Usual adult PO/IV 20–40 mg/day; pediatric PO 0.5–1 mg/kg/day (common max 20 mg/day in esophagitis/GERD) by indication.
indications:
## Indications

- Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and esophagitis.
- Peptic ulcer; *H. pylori* eradication in combination regimens.
- NSAID gastropathy prevention/treatment; upper GI bleeding (hospital IV phase).
- Hypersecretory states / Zollinger–Ellison (high doses).

## Precautions

- Interactions: atazanavir (contraindicated), iron, itraconazole/ketoconazole/voriconazole, digoxin, clopidogrel (debated), rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, diazepam.
- Long-term use: hypomagnesemia, GI infection risk, fractures (chronic context).

> Prefer PO as soon as tolerated; IV is a hospital bridge.

adulto.dose: GERD/ulcer: **20 mg PO every 24 h** (up to 40 mg/day by severity). Hypersecretion/Zollinger–Ellison: start **60 mg/day** (titrate; may divide every 8–12 h). IV: **40 mg every 24 h** (in UGIB often 40 mg every 8–12 h for first days per institutional regimen, then space).
adulto.administration: Prefer PO fasting; do not chew granules. IV: reconstitute only with manufacturer solvent; for infusion dilute to ~0.4 mg/mL and infuse 20–30 min.
adulto.notes: Reconstituted injectable: limited stability (e.g. 4 h). With 0.9% NaCl diluted ~12 h; with 5% dextrose ~6 h (check label).

pediatrico.presentation: Capsules/tablets 10–20–40 mg; MUPS 10–20 mg; vial 40 mg; PO suspension (e.g. 2 mg/mL with bicarbonate by brand).
pediatrico.dose: PO esophagitis: **0.5 mg/kg/dose every 24 h** (max **20 mg/day**). Duodenal ulcer: **1 mg/kg/day** every 12 h (max 20 mg/day). GERD ≥ 1 month: **0.5–1 mg/kg/dose every 24 h** (max 20 mg/day). IV 1 month–12 years: **0.5–2 mg/kg/dose every 24 h**; > 12 years: **40 mg every 24 h**. UGIB: every 8 h × 3–5 days by course, then every 12–24 h.
pediatrico.administration: PO; capsule may be opened and granules mixed with yogurt/juice (do not chew). NG: bicarbonate/MUPS techniques per protocol. IV as in adult.
pediatrico.notes: Switch to PO as soon as oral tolerance allows.

neonatal.dose: Symptomatic GERD under neonatology: often **0.5–1 mg/kg/day PO** (similar IV range 0.5–1 mg/kg/day); confirm local protocol — off-label in many settings.
neonatal.notes: Consider differential diagnosis of vomiting; not routine for physiologic regurgitation.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Reconstituted IV: use within manufacturer window (usually hours at room temperature).
- Reconstituted suspension: per label beyond-use date after opening.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Headache, diarrhea, nausea, constipation, abdominal pain, vomiting, dizziness. Rare: interstitial nephritis, hypersensitivity.
